title: Tencent Hy4: New AI Model With Computer Use (2026)
summary: Tencent Hy4 performs software tasks on behalf of users, though testing remains confined to controlled lab settings with no real-world validation yet.
body_markdown:
## Hy4 performance on three automation tasks


3.2 seconds against 0.9: that is what Hy4 took on three small automation tasks, where it matched GPT-5.4-mini on correctness, **at about eight times the cost per task** .


### The three tasks and how they were scored


On 2026-11-18 tencent/hy4 and openai/gpt-5.4-mini were run through[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/tencent/hy4) , a gateway that serves both models behind one API, on default settings. Hy4's defaults reason before answering. The tasks were:


- Sort a support ticket
- Pull fields from an invoice
- Summarise an email thread


To score them, each result was checked against a known answer. Three tasks make a smoke test, not a benchmark, so a pass here shows only that a model handles easy, well-defined work.


### Results, speed and cost per task


Since both models got every task right, the difference between them is speed and price. That's the gap a team already running a cheap model would have to justify.


tencent/hy4 got 3 of 3 right. It had a median of 3.2 seconds and a cost of $0.0012 per task. openai/gpt-5.4-mini also got 3 of 3 right, with a median of 0.9 seconds and a cost of $0.000142 per task.


Three tasks, one tie on accuracy: that tells you very little. You **can't reliably say which performs better** .


At thousands of tickets a day, the speed and cost columns are what would compound: a workflow waiting 3.2 seconds per step feels sluggish, and the bill is roughly eight times larger.


Since Hy4 reasons before it answers, some of its delay probably comes from that, so a rerun with that behaviour reduced, if the endpoint allows it, would be the fairer follow-up.
